text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- U.S. Congressman Lane Evans says the United States is developing a programme aimed at helping Vietnam overcome the consequences of war, particularly those caused by bombs and mines.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet has been impressed with a timber processing factory in Laos, saying it could provide a model for Vietnam's forestry industry.
-- The South Korean conglomerate Daewoo plans to invest $1 billion in an aluminium casting joint-venture in the central highland province of Daklak.
-- The State Bank and Finance Ministry have proposed giving another $25 million to 18 state corporations.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet has concluded his official friendship visit to Laos.
-- Deputy Prime Minister Phan Van Khai has called for stronger development of the tourism and hotel industries.
-- The Vietnam Customs Office has discovered and confiscated seven tonnes of illegal narcotics since January 1993.
-- Districts in Ho Chi Minh City are reinforcing environmental management and protection measures.
-- Communist Party senior politburo member, Le Kha Phieu, says that action against drugs is the task for the entire people, with the customs office and police being the key forces.
